title: Homepage visual world: Frentex Tech
question: One direction for the new homepage and the site's signature. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Waybill
options.lineage: Shipment waybills and parcel tracking: the Jeddah-port and courier tracking pages every Saudi business already checks daily
options.thesis: Your business requests, tracked like a shipment: one request, stamped at every system it passes through.
materials: printed waybill form grid in brand-blue ink
a tracking number that threads every page
options.viewport: Headline and the conversation CTA on the right; on the left a full-height blue waybill where request FX-014 is stamped through four checkpoints in sequence: website form, then مدار (CRM), then سير (approval), then رصيد (purchase order), with the fields it carries visibly passed along.
options.risk: If the label grammar gets literal (barcodes, courier logos), Frentex reads as a logistics company. The tracking is a metaphor for requests, never parcels.

raised.raise: Every checkpoint is addressable: each stamp opens the live demo of that system, so reading the route is also how you try it.
Absence is designed: checkpoints a request has not reached are ghost stamps, and 'returned for completion' is a designed state, not an error.
Every illustrative datum carries an origin ticket, so the honesty disclosure is part of the label grammar instead of fine print.
The page is ruled as one continuous route line down the whole homepage, with tabular timestamps at each stop.
Colour rationed to the moving edge: amber marks only the live checkpoint; everything else stays blue ink on white.
Total commitment of the field: the waybill is a drenched brand-blue region owning half the first viewport, not blue accents on a white template.

options.label: The Line Map
options.lineage: Riyadh Metro and transit diagram notation
options.thesis: Your systems as stations on one line: a request rides from the website to the purchase order, changing hands at interchanges.
options.viewport: A line diagram crossing the first viewport with four stations (الموقع, مدار, سير, رصيد) and a moving token; the headline sits in the map legend box.
options.risk: Familiar: 'connections = metro map' is where many integration sites land, and it shows the route but not what each stop does.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Each system as a card in one stack, linked by painted buttons.
options.viewport: A stack of four system cards; a button flips to the next system.
options.case: Fuses poorly: Saudi SME owners have no memory of HyperCard, and one-bit black breaks the blue-and-white identity.
options.kept: Every checkpoint is addressable and opens its live demo.

options.label: Seven-Segment Totem
options.thesis: Request counts and statuses lit as segment digits.
options.viewport: A price-totem stack showing requests per system.
options.case: Loses both axes: digits show volume, not how systems connect, and the dark LED ground drops the brand.
options.kept: Designed absence: ghost stamps for unreached checkpoints and a designed 'returned' state.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Systems as stalls trading data by origin.
options.viewport: A moonlit lane of system stalls.
options.case: Loses both axes: whimsy undercuts the enterprise credibility goal.
options.kept: An origin ticket on every illustrative datum.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: The business drawn in section, the request as a moving beam.
options.viewport: A long building section with a room per system.
options.case: Loses both axes: architecture is a step removed from software for an SME owner.
options.kept: One continuous route line ruled down the page, with tabular timestamps.

options.label: Sliding House
options.thesis: Sliding planes reconfigure one space into connected systems.
options.viewport: Planes slide to join website, CRM and ERP panels.
options.case: Close on clarity, loses on audience: De Stijl is a design-insider reference and its primaries break the brand.
options.kept: Colour rationed to the moving edge: amber only on the live checkpoint.

options.label: Highlife Sleeve
options.thesis: Exuberant painted lettering over saturated colour fields.
options.viewport: A painted headline over tropical fields.
options.case: Loses both axes: no tie to the audience or to systems.
options.kept: Total commitment of the field: a drenched blue waybill region.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean B2B software-agency homepage, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and two CTAs beside a product screenshot, then a services grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other agency in the Gulf, by design.
